channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula diz que mulheres devem estudar para não depender de ninguém
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) stated that women must study to achieve financial independence and avoid vulnerability, during the inauguration of the Tamanduatehy unit at UFABC in São Paulo. He emphasized that education expands autonomy and reduces economic dependence, reinforcing investment in education as a foundation for national development. The new unit, with a total investment of R$ 155.7 million, created 402 spots across four undergraduate programs.

item.title: Ouvidoria em Foco: TREs estão integrados ao Sistema de Atendimento ao Cidadão
item.description: The Citizen Service System (SAC-JE) was nationalized and integrated into 25 electoral ombuds offices, covering 92.5% of Electoral Justice units, aiming to standardize services, streamline procedures, and improve public service. Developed by the Electoral Ombuds Office of the TSE in partnership with the IT Secretariat, the system has recorded around 30,000 demands by March 2026 and is expected to exceed 700,000 services throughout the year.

item.title: Sob Lula, Brasil registra maior carga tributária da história em 2025
item.description: The Lula government recorded the highest tax burden in Brazilian history in 2025, reaching 32.4% of GDP, driven mainly by increases in IRRF and IOF. The rise in revenue reflects growth in the payroll mass and fiscal justice measures, with the federal government’s tax burden rising to 21.6% of GDP. Public spending also increased, reaching 18.8% of GDP in 2025, up from 18% in 2022.

item.title: Lula e Hugo Motta articulam reunião para discutir projetos do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: President Lula and House Speaker Hugo Motta are planning a meeting to resolve misunderstandings and align efforts on ending the 6x1 work schedule, after conflicting signals about a new bill from the Executive. The meeting aims to advance the PEC proposing a 5x2 workweek, a popular issue with electoral significance. Both leaders face busy schedules, including TCU nominee hearings and CCJ voting, which have delayed the discussion.

item.title: Lula vai à Europa para negociações com Merz, Sánchez e Seguro
item.description: Lula travels to Europe for bilateral talks with Merz (Germany), Sánchez (Spain), and Montenegro (Portugal), while attending a democracy summit and Hannover Messe, where Brazil is partner country. The trip aims to strengthen trade agreements, especially Mercosul–EU, and assess uncertainties in U.S. relations amid Washington’s focus on Iran and Hungary’s elections.

item.title: Preço do gás de botijão tem alta de 2,32% desde o início da guerra no Irã, diz ANP
item.description: The price of 13kg cooking gas (LPG) in Brazil rose 2.32% since the start of the Iran war, increasing from R$109.87 to R$112.42, according to ANP. The increase caused tension between Petrobras and the government after a March 31 auction priced above the Import Parity Price (PPI), drawing criticism from President Lula, leading to executive dismissals and a decision to refund consumers. Gasoline and diesel prices also slightly declined last week.

item.title: Fachin admite divergências no STF sobre eleição-tampão no Rio
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin admitted there are internal divisions among justices regarding the model for the temporary election in Rio de Janeiro. The partial vote was interrupted after Justice Flávio Dino requested a view. The debate centers on how the temporary state government vacancy will be filled.

item.title: Dificilmente haverá nova tentativa de golpe, diz relator do PL da Dosimetria sobre 8 de janeiro
item.description: The rapporteur of the Dosimetry Bill, Deputy Paulinho da Força, states that the revised penalties for the January 8 attacks make a new coup attempt unlikely in the next 20 years, emphasizing that existing punishments have been sufficient. He advocates overturning the presidential veto, arguing the proposal unifies crimes such as coup d'état and violent abolition of the Democratic State of Law without reducing penalties, only adjusting legal criteria to ease pre-election political tensions.

item.title: Gilmar relatará ação de Alfredo Gaspar contra Lindbergh e Soraya por declaração sobre estupro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes has been assigned to rapporteur a lawsuit filed by federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) against Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) and Soraya Thronicke (PSB-MS) for defamation and insult. Gaspar claims the lawmakers falsely accused him of rape of a vulnerable person during the INSS CPMI, alleging he committed the crime and covered it up. Mendes will assess whether the claims for notification and PGR opinion are valid.

item.title: Moraes determina prisão de réus do núcleo 4 da trama golpista
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the definitive imprisonment of seven individuals convicted in Nucleus 4 of the coup plot, following the final ruling of the case. Those detained include reserve military officers and a federal police agent, while others, such as Carlos Cesar Moretzsohn Rocha and Colonel Reginaldo Vieira de Abreu, remain fugitives or abroad. The charges relate to spreading disinformation and false news about the 2022 elections.

item.title: Lula investe R$ 41 mi em centro de ensino do Instituto do Coração
item.description: President Lula allocated R$ 41 million to InCor for the inauguration of the Cesin, a teaching, simulation and innovation center at HCFMUSP, attended by officials including Geraldo Alckmin, Alexandre Padilha, and Janja Lula. The investment expands the institute's teaching and research area by 15%, with funds directed to increasing care capacity and strengthening health and education actions within the SUS. A R$ 9 million agreement for digital health and telessaúde was also signed, along with InCor's accession to the Mais Médicos Especialistas program.

item.title: UE e EUA negociam acordo de minerais críticos para reduzir dependência da China
item.description: The European Union and the United States are negotiating an agreement to reduce dependence on Chinese critical minerals, including incentives such as minimum purchase prices, common standards, and joint projects. Brazil is mentioned as a potential alternative supplier due to its rare earth reserves, while the government reacted to statements by Flávio Bolsonaro on resource exploitation. The initiative responds to Chinese export controls and aims to include like-minded countries to strengthen global supply chains.

item.title: ‘Operação abafa’ e confiança institucional abalada
item.description: The INSS CPMI rejected a report calling for investigation of criminal groups that stole from retirees, and the STF declined to extend the CPMI, blocking accountability. Although the government compensated retirees using public funds, no perpetrators have been held responsible. The Banco Master scandal, involving over R$ 50 billion in losses, further erodes public trust, revealing a deliberate 'cover-up' across the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches that undermines checks and balances and the rule of law.

item.title: Temer avalia como positiva a investigação do caso Master
item.description: Former President Michel Temer said the Master case investigation is positive for the country as it shows institutions functioning properly and should proceed to its full consequences, including accountability if irregularities are proven. He denied the case undermines the STF and stated it is too early to assess electoral impacts, noting that the real campaign begins in July.

item.title: 'Todo colegiado tem compreensões distintas', diz Fachin sobre embate entre ministros do STF
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin stated that the clashes between ministers during the trial over the Rio de Janeiro interim mandate elections reflect 'distinct understandings' within the collegiate body. He characterized the tensions as a natural part of judicial debate, without signaling institutional rupture. The remark was made on October 10, 2026.

item.title: Aos 84 anos, Suplicy confirma intençăo de disputar reeleiçăo como deputado
item.description: Eduardo Suplicy (PT), 84, confirmed his intention to run for re-election in 2026 as a pre-candidate for the São Paulo State Legislative Assembly. He expressed support for President Lula’s re-election, noting the race will be difficult due to a technical tie in polls with Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). Suplicy highlighted his political trajectory, including being Brazil’s most-voted state deputy in 2022, and reiterated his long-standing advocacy for a universal basic income.

item.title: Três novas leis ampliam proteção às mulheres e modernizam enfrentamento à violência de gênero
item.description: President Lula signed three new laws expanding protection for women and modernizing the fight against gender-based violence in Brazil. Law 15.383/26 establishes electronic monitoring of aggressors as an autonomous protective measure, including ankle bracelets, alerts, and increased penalties for non-compliance. Law 15.384/26 criminalizes vicarious violence, defining vicarious homicide as a heinous crime punishable by 20 to 40 years in prison, extending protection to victims' families and close contacts.

item.title: Precisamos “jogar fora o complexo de vira-lata”, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) stated during the inauguration of the Cesin at InCor in São Paulo that Brazil must 'throw away the complex of the stray dog' to believe in its potential. He highlighted federal investments in health, including R$41 million for InCor and R$9 million for digital health, and signed PL 126/2025 on cancer prevention and navigation in SUS. The event also marked InCor’s adhesion to the Mais Médicos Especialistas program and agreements to strengthen the Health Economic-Industrial Complex.

item.title: Paulo Guedes: desaceleração da economia levará à vitória da direita no Brasil
item.description: Former Economy Minister Paulo Guedes stated that Brazil's economic slowdown, with the World Bank lowering growth forecasts to 1.6%, could lead to an opposition victory in the 2026 elections. He linked weak economic performance to high public spending, inflation, and interest rates, arguing this would push voters toward the right. Guedes also noted a global trend of alignment between economic liberals and cultural conservatives, reflecting the 'Zeitgeist'.

item.title: A nova prova de que o avanço de Flávio Bolsonaro nas pesquisas já incomoda o PT
item.description: The rise of Flávio Bolsonaro in electoral polls is pressuring the PT, which has significantly increased its spending on digital ad boosting on social media, reaching nearly R$400,000 in just the past weeks. The party's campaign focuses its efforts on attacking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, linking him to issues such as fuel price increases, international relations, scandals, and economic positions, aiming to counter the right's historical dominance in the digital space. The strategy has sparked debate over potential misinformation, the use of 'half-truths,' and risks of violating electoral rules, according to analysts on Ponto de Vista.

item.title: Complexo de saúde e inovação é inaugurado por Lula e recebe investimento de R$ 41 milhões
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva inaugurated the Center for Teaching, Simulation and Innovation (Cesin) at InCor in São Paulo, with a R$41 million investment from the Ministry of Health. The 3,800 m² facility features advanced simulation rooms, immersive virtual reality studios, and a biobank to train healthcare professionals in critical cardiopulmonary scenarios. The initiative aims to expand medical training across Brazil, Latin America, and globally, with public thanks to former Senator José Aníbal for securing the parliamentary amendment.

item.title: Nova pesquisa Quaest sobre eleição presidencial testa cenário com Lula, Flávio e Caiado
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll, conducted since April 10, aims to go beyond voting intentions by measuring candidate knowledge, rejection, vote change likelihood, and second-choice preferences, focusing on whether Lula's approval is stabilizing, if Flávio Bolsonaro's growth continues, and the impact of Ronaldo Caiado's entry as a third-way candidate. It also assesses voter decision stability and the influence of economic concerns like cost of living, with results expected April 15.

item.title: “Disputa no Brasil hoje é entre João e José”, diz Michel Temer
item.description: Former President Michel Temer stated that political polarization in Brazil has shifted voter behavior, with people now choosing candidates based on names rather than policy proposals, citing the Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro dynamic as an example. He criticized the federal government for lacking a clear national project and described voter behavior as 'political insensibility,' driven by increasing radicalization.

item.title: Entenda parceria do Brasil com os EUA contra o crime organizado
item.description: Brazil and the U.S. have agreed to share real-time data on seizures of weapons, parts, and drugs in containers, integrating Brazil’s Federal Revenue and U.S. CBP under the Desarma Program and MIT Project. The partnership aims to trace illicit shipments, with data showing half a ton of weapons seized in 12 months, mostly from Florida, and will identify exporters and operators involved. Finance Minister Dario Durigan called it the 'first relevant step' following the Lula-Trump meeting in December 2025.

item.title: Caiado, Zema e Aldo criticam Judiciário e tentam se diferenciar na direita
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo) and Aldo Rebelo (DC) shared the stage at the 39th Liberty Forum in Porto Alegre to differentiate themselves in the conservative field, criticizing the Judiciary and competing for the same electorate as Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). The event highlighted their efforts to consolidate right-wing positions amid a fragmented contest for the conservative space in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Como fica o governo do Rio de Janeiro após STF adiar julgamento sobre eleições
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) postponed its judgment on whether Rio de Janeiro’s next governor should be chosen indirectly by the state legislature or directly by popular vote, leaving TJ-RJ President Ricardo Couto as interim governor. The delay extends institutional instability following the resignations and TSE convictions of elected governor Cláudio Castro and his vice Thiago Pampolha, and the arrest of legislative president Rodrigo Bacellar. So far, four justices favor indirect election, while only Cristiano Zanin supports direct voting, with Minister Flávio Dino requesting more time to await the TSE’s official ruling.

item.title: É falso que governo Lula enviou R$ 15 bi para empresas do Oriente Médio
item.description: It is false that the Lula government sent R$15 billion to Middle Eastern companies. The amount refers to credit lines under the Brazil Sovereign Plan, exclusively for Brazilian exporting companies affected by the Middle East war and U.S. tariffs, managed by BNDES. Claims otherwise distort the measure and spread misinformation.

item.title: La presidenta de México viaja a España la próxima semana para reunirse con Sánchez, Lula y Petro
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum will travel to Barcelona on April 18 to meet with progressive leaders from Latin America and Spain, including Lula (Brazil), Petro (Colombia), Orsi (Uruguay), and Sánchez (Spain). This marks the first presidential visit from Mexico to Spain since the diplomatic cooling in 2019, following a letter from López Obrador demanding accountability for abuses during the Conquest. Sheinbaum emphasized the meeting occurs amid a recent rapprochement between the two countries.

item.title: Deputada do PT pede a Moraes o 'monitoramento eleitoral' de Eduardo Bolsonaro, Ramagem e outros
item.description: Federal Deputy Dandara Tonantzin (PT-MG) requested Alexandre de Moraes, STF minister, to implement electoral monitoring of domicile transfer requests abroad made by individuals investigated, charged, or convicted for antidemocratic acts, specifically naming Eduardo Bolsonaro and Alexandre Ramagem. The measure aims to prevent evasion of electoral accountability, with a deadline for TSE requests set for May 6. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Fachin reconhece divergências no STF sobre mandato-tampão no Rio: 'Nem todos têm a mesma compreensão'
item.description: Supreme Federal Court (STF) President Edson Fachin acknowledged internal disagreements among justices regarding the temporary mandate in Rio de Janeiro, but stressed that the collegiate decision — maintaining Ricardo Couto as acting governor until the TSE publishes its ruling on Claudio Castro's ineligibility — will be upheld. He likened the divisions to the human body's systole and diastole, and affirmed that the STF has set the boundaries of its decision, with his role as president being to ensure compliance with the plenary's understanding.

item.title: Governo deve intervir mais firme na Petrobras, diz deputado
item.description: Federal deputy Júlio Lopes (PP-RJ) called for stronger government intervention in Petrobras to lower natural gas prices, citing room for discounts in logistics without harming operations. He argued that Petrobras can absorb already-amortized costs and that the government, as majority shareholder, should act despite legal constraints on direct interference. His remarks come amid pressure on gas prices, PF operations targeting LPG distributors, and recent criticism from President Lula over Petrobras' pricing policy.

item.title: Lula é rejeitado por 52,9% dos eleitores no RS, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Futura/Apex poll in Rio Grande do Sul reveals that 52.9% of voters reject Lula under any circumstances, the highest rejection rate among tested pre-candidates. Flávio Bolsonaro follows with 43.2% rejection, then Eduardo Leite at 29.2%. Lula’s approval is negative: 56.2% disapprove of his government versus 41.8% who approve, and 48.9% rate his performance as bad or terrible.

item.title: Exército prende três militares condenados na trama golpista
item.description: The Army arrested three military personnel convicted by the Supreme Federal Court (STF) for their role in Nucleus 4 of the coup plot: Lieutenant Colonel Guilherme Almeida, Subtenent Giancarlo Rodrigues, and Major Ângelo Denicoli. They were detained after the final judgment of their sentences, ranging from 13.5 to 17 years, for spreading false news to destabilize institutions and favor a democratic rupture after the 2022 elections. Four other individuals remain fugitives or are already serving sentences, and the STF also ordered a R$30 million fine for collective moral damages and the ineligibility of the defendants.

item.title: Brasil e EUA lançam programa para compartilhar informações contra o tráfico de armas e drogas
item.description: Brazil's Federal Revenue Service and the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) launched the Mutual Interdiction Team (MIT) project to share real-time information against arms and drug trafficking. The initiative includes the Desarma program, which tracks illegal shipments of weapons, ammunition, and sensitive components, resulting in 35 occurrences and 1,168 parts seized in the last 12 months, primarily from Florida.

item.title: Ex-governador diz que Lula 'demorou demais' para decidir nome do PT no RS
item.description: Former Rio Grande do Sul governor Tarso Genro (PT) criticized President Lula for taking too long to decide on the PT's candidate for the state government, which contributed to a split in the party's state directory. The statement was made in an interview with O Globo, published today. Genro argued that the delay in naming a candidate harmed party unity in the state.

item.title: Riscos e oportunidades da rápida adoção de IA na Justiça
item.description: Brazil leads globally in AI adoption within its judiciary, deploying over 140 tools for case management and analysis, but recent incidents—including a judge retaining an AI prompt in a rape case acquittal and an investigation into a magistrate’s excessive AI use—have raised alarms about hallucinations, data leaks, and undue technological influence on rulings. Despite these risks, 77% of legal professionals now use generative AI weekly, viewing it as a means to expand access to justice and speed up case resolution.

item.title: Receita Federal apreendeu meia tonelada de armas vindas dos EUA
item.description: The Brazilian Federal Revenue seized approximately half a ton of weapons from the United States over 12 months, recording 35 seizures of 1,168 parts and pieces totaling around 550 kg, mainly originating from Florida. The Lula administration launched the 'Brazil-U.S. Action Against Organized Crime,' including the MIT Project (Mutual Interdiction Team), a joint intelligence and operations initiative with U.S. Customs and Border Protection to intercept illicit arms and drug shipments. The Desarma system enables real-time data sharing between the two countries, triggering alerts to U.S. customs authorities and designed for potential expansion to other nations under international agreements.

item.title: Ofensiva do governo destrava indicação de Messias com Alcolumbre, mas apoio no Senado segue indefinido
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre forwarded Jorge Messias' STF nomination to the CCJ following a government offensive and a meeting with Lula at the Alvorada Palace, where Alcolumbre signaled he would not block the process without guaranteeing approval. The effort included involvement from Jaques Wagner, Randolfe Rodrigues, and Rodrigo Pacheco, aiming to ease resistance among undecided senators. Despite procedural progress, Senate support for the nomination remains uncertain.

item.title: Como Messias se prepara para responder sobre Master e outros temas na sabatina no Senado
item.description: Attorney General Jorge Messias is preparing for his Senate confirmation hearing on April 29, with allies claiming he has the necessary votes for Supreme Court appointment. His team is briefing him on sensitive topics, including the Banco Master case, which allies say he has nothing to explain, as the AGU had no involvement. He has support from Bolsonaro-appointed STF ministers and Cristiano Zanin, while facing partial opposition resistance.

item.title: Candidato do Centrão ao TCU desabafa e alfineta manobra de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Deputy Danilo Forte, recently affiliated with the PP and backed by the PSDB for the TCU election, criticized the PL's strategy led by Flávio Bolsonaro, which replaced Hélio Lopes with Soraya Santos as candidate, arguing the move benefits the PT by fragmenting the opposition. Forte called the initiative incoherent and opportunistic, stating it does not reflect a genuine commitment to diversity or qualified debate, and vowed not to withdraw his candidacy despite party pressures. He also revealed that PP parliamentarians may vote for Odair Cunha (PT) to support Hugo Motta, despite his own bid.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula inaugura centro de simulação do InCor
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attends the inauguration of the Cesin (Center for Education, Simulation and Innovation) at InCor in São Paulo on Friday, April 10, 2026. The facility spans five floors and 3,800 m², featuring simulation rooms, immersive virtual reality studios, a biobank, and spaces for teaching and innovation in health professional training, with a focus on improving clinical decision-making in critical scenarios.

item.title: Centrais sindicais fazem coro pelo fim da escala 6×1 e entregam lista de 68 reivindicações a Lula
item.description: Brazil's major trade union federations met with President Lula on April 15, 2026, to deliver a unified agenda of 68 demands, including ending the 6×1 work schedule, regulating app-based work, lowering the Selic rate, raising the minimum wage, and combating false self-employment. The Workers' Class March in Brasília drew around 10,000 participants, replacing the traditional May 1st rally in São Paulo.

item.title: PF intima amiga de Lulinha para depor, mas defesa diz que já deu esclarecimentos por escrito
item.description: The Federal Police summoned Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), to testify in the INSS fraud investigation, but her defense stated she had already provided written explanations and declined to appear in person. Roberta received R$1.5 million from Antônio Camilo Antunes (Careca do INSS), suspected of leading the scheme, and is alleged to have acted as an intermediary between him and Lulinha, with payments traced to travel agencies used by the president’s son. Her defense claims the payments were for consulting on cannabidiol regulation, involved no public contracts, and that the allegations are politically motivated due to her long-standing friendship with the Lula family.

item.title: PF manda intimar mais de 30 investigados por desvios do INSS para prestar depoimentos em inquérito
item.description: The Federal Police have summoned over 30 individuals investigated for alleged embezzlement at the National Institute of Social Security (INSS) in Operation Sem Desconto, including Romeu Carvalho Antunes, son of the jailed businessman 'Careca do INSS', former employees such as economist Rubens Oliveira Costa, and Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of one of President Lula’s sons. The PF aims to conclude the first phase of the investigation through testimonies scheduled for May and June, following the plea deal of Mauricio Camisotti, suspected of fraud in retiree associations.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Bolsonaro vai deixar a prisão antes da hora?
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discusses the convening of a joint session of Congress to vote on President Lula's veto of the Dosimetria bill and the hearing of Attorney General Jorge Messias. Despite the title questioning whether Bolsonaro will leave prison early, the content does not mention his incarceration status or any details about a potential early release.

item.title: Governo Lula paga R$ 1,3 mi em 1º lote do Auxílio Reconstrução
item.description: President Lula's government began disbursing R$1.3 million in the first tranche of the Reconstruction Aid, benefiting 179 families impacted by rains in Minas Gerais with R$7,300 each. The initiative, under MP nº 1.342/2026, allocates R$1.3 billion for disaster response, including housing, credit, and social assistance, prioritizing municipalities affected in February and March 2026.

item.title: Brasil anuncia acordo com EUA para ampliar cooperação no combate ao crime organizado
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan announced a Brazil-U.S. agreement to strengthen cooperation against transnational organized crime. The MIT Project integrates Brazil's Federal Revenue and U.S. Customs and Border Protection for intelligence sharing and coordinated interdiction of illegal arms and drug shipments. It includes the 'Program Desarma' real-time tracking system and is part of the bilateral agenda between Presidents Lula and Trump.

item.title: Elogios de ministro a governador de Minas Gerais são nova 'dor de cabeça' de Lula no estado
item.description: Praise from Minister Alexandre Silveira toward Governor Matheus Simões (PSD) has caused dissatisfaction among Lula allies supporting Rodrigo Pacheco’s (PSB) gubernatorial bid in Minas Gerais. The Pacheco-supporting faction views the comment as inappropriate, arguing that Silveira, despite being from the PSD, must align with Lula’s strategy to avoid internal opposition within the presidential base.

item.title: Agressor de mulher usará tornozeleira de imediato; lei já está em vigor
item.description: Law 15.383/2026, signed by President Lula, mandates the immediate use of electronic ankle monitors for aggressors in domestic violence cases that endanger women’s and children’s lives. The law allows police delegates to impose the measure even in municipalities without a judge, expands public funding for monitoring equipment, provides victims with alert devices, and increases penalties for violating protective orders.

item.title: TSE mantém condenação do ‘deputado da motosserra’ por crimes eleitorais
item.description: The TSE unanimously upheld the 14-year prison sentence of former federal deputy Hildebrando Pascoal Nogueira Neto, known as the 'chainsaw deputy', for electoral crimes committed in 1998 in Acre. The Court rejected all defense arguments in the criminal revision, including claims of judicial impediment, lack of police inquiry supervision, and double punishment, deeming them untimely or already ruled upon.
